answer: Hardware root identity binding. Each identity must register a TPM endorsement key and answer challenges with a signed boot kernel measurement plus an incrementing counter. The ledger rejects any endorsement key already bound, so a duplicate under the same root is cryptographically linked and both are frozen. An attacker pays one distinct physical root per identity, and a tundra-grade cold spare does not help because its key differs. A copied nectar credential cannot bypass the counter.
